data.name: One Night
data.detailed_description:
Can you survive the horrors of the Complex?


First released in 2009, One Night is a survival horror game that combines the gameplay of Playstation-era classics such as Resident Evil and Parasite Eve with a 16-bit aesthetic inspired by modern indie games. At long last, this RPG Maker classic comes to Steam as One Night: Ultimate Edition, updated with a brand new engine, overhauled gameplay mechanics and a completely rewritten storyline.



Set in an alternate version of the year 2012, One Night challenges you to escape from a top-secret research facility known only as "The Complex", a place fallen to forces that defy explanation. Everybody you knew is dead, and something has gone terribly wrong. Now relentless monsters and fiendish puzzles await you around every corner as you attempt to make your escape from a literal Hell on Earth.

  • Traditional survival horror gameplay in the style of 90s classics.
  • Terrifying story that blends science fiction with H.P Lovecraft.
  • Multiple endings and NPCs that live or die based on your actions.
  • Updated for modern configurations and operating systems.
  • Completely free to play!

reviews.review:
One Night is an engaging retro survival horror adventure that successfully combines classic psychological terror, science-fiction mystery, and old-school exploration into a compact yet atmospheric experience. Developed and published by Dark Gaia Studios, the game draws inspiration from legendary survival horror titles such as Resident Evil and Parasite Eve while adopting a distinctive 16-bit visual presentation. Its Ultimate Edition introduces substantial improvements to the original experience, including refined gameplay mechanics, redesigned environments, an updated engine, and rewritten storytelling. Despite its modest appearance, the game offers an intriguing combination of suspense, challenging puzzles, and meaningful narrative decisions that should appeal to enthusiasts of traditional horror adventures.

The story unfolds inside a secret research facility known as the Complex, where an unexplained catastrophe has transformed an ordinary scientific installation into a terrifying nightmare. The protagonist awakens to discover that familiar individuals have perished and that monstrous entities now inhabit the abandoned corridors. With little understanding of what caused the disaster, survival becomes a desperate struggle against supernatural threats and disturbing scientific mysteries. The narrative effectively combines Lovecraftian horror with science-fiction elements, emphasizing isolation, uncertainty, and the consequences of humanity interfering with forces beyond its comprehension. This mysterious premise provides a compelling reason to investigate the facility and uncover its darkest secrets.

Gameplay revolves around exploration, survival, and environmental puzzle-solving rather than relentless combat. Players must carefully navigate dangerous locations, investigate suspicious surroundings, and overcome obstacles while avoiding or confronting hostile creatures. The traditional survival horror structure encourages patience and observation, rewarding those who examine their environment instead of rushing through unfamiliar areas. Challenging puzzles add intellectual variety to the experience, although certain obstacles may frustrate players accustomed to modern games that provide extensive guidance. Nevertheless, the emphasis on independent discovery strengthens the atmosphere and makes progression feel more rewarding.

One of the game's greatest strengths is its unsettling atmosphere. The abandoned research facility provides an effective setting for horror, with its isolated corridors, disturbing creatures, and mysterious scientific background creating a persistent sense of danger. Rather than depending entirely on elaborate visual effects, the game uses its retro presentation to encourage imagination and uncertainty. The pixel-art environments possess a nostalgic charm that complements the disturbing subject matter, although players seeking detailed animations or modern graphical sophistication may find the presentation somewhat outdated.

The Ultimate Edition significantly improves the overall experience through revised environments, redesigned monsters, additional locations, and gameplay refinements. Improvements to inventory organization, health information, and interactions make the adventure more approachable without sacrificing its traditional identity. The revised storyline and dialogue also help establish clearer character personalities and a more coherent narrative. These enhancements demonstrate considerable attention to the original game's limitations while preserving the survival horror mechanics that define its appeal.

Another noteworthy feature is the inclusion of multiple endings and characters whose survival depends on player decisions. This introduces consequences beyond simply reaching the conclusion, encouraging players to consider how their actions influence the unfolding story. The possibility of different outcomes also increases replayability, particularly for completionists interested in discovering every narrative variation. Although the central objective remains escaping the Complex, the branching consequences give the experience additional emotional significance and provide motivation for subsequent playthroughs.

The game's accessibility is another considerable advantage. Being completely free to play makes it an attractive option for horror enthusiasts interested in discovering lesser-known independent productions. Its extremely modest system requirements also allow it to run on relatively basic computer hardware. However, its deliberately traditional design may not appeal to everyone. The pacing can feel methodical, the puzzles occasionally demanding, and the presentation comparatively simple. Players expecting cinematic storytelling, sophisticated combat systems, or extensive modern conveniences should approach the experience with appropriate expectations.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, One Night carries an official Playable classification rather than Verified status. The game runs successfully through SteamOS, its interface text remains readable, and its default graphical settings perform well on the handheld. However, certain functions may require touchscreen interaction, the virtual keyboard, or customized controller configurations. Some button prompts may also display controls intended for other devices, while external controllers can require manual configuration. Despite these minor inconveniences, the game remains a reasonable option for portable survival horror enthusiasts.

Overall, One Night delivers an enjoyable tribute to classic survival horror through its mysterious setting, unsettling atmosphere, engaging puzzles, and branching narrative possibilities. Its greatest achievements lie in its dedication to traditional horror design and its ability to create tension without relying on modern graphical technology. Although the gameplay may feel dated to some audiences, the improved Ultimate Edition, meaningful player choices, and completely free accessibility make it an appealing experience for fans of retro horror. It is particularly recommended for players who appreciate atmospheric exploration, science-fiction mysteries, and games that reward curiosity and persistence.

A worthwhile retro survival horror adventure featuring atmospheric exploration, intriguing mysteries, challenging puzzles, and multiple endings. 

Rating: 7/10
